title: March All-Hands - Q1 Updates
customer_attendees: People Ops, Eng, Product, Sales, Research
summary: Company all-hands covering Q1 performance, strategic bets for next quarter (Private deployments, Dedicated growth, Optimize tooling), hiring plan, and security/compliance milestones. Leadership answered questions and closed with next steps for team leads and managers.
next_steps: Leadership to share detailed Q1 metrics deck by 2026-03-26
People Ops to publish updated hiring plan and interview scorecards by 2026-03-30
Product to circulate Private deployment rollout timeline (internal) by 2026-03-29
Engineering to prioritize two latency improvements for Redwood runtime; status update at next engineering all-hands
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 10:00 AM - 11:00 AM PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (CEO), Maya Alvarez (CTO), Liam Patel (VP Eng), Noah Kim (Head Product), Olivia Ruiz (Head Sales), Priya Shah (People Ops), plus ~150 staff

[00:00] Avery Chen: all right, uh, thanks everyone for joining the March all hands uh we're gonna kick off, start with a quick company update and then we'll go into product and security. we are tight on time so we'll try to keep sections to 10-12 minutes each, and then q and a at the end.

[00:28] Maya Alvarez: quick note - shout out to the infra team, they shipped the multi-region routing change last week which cut p95 tail by about 12% for hosted API, so big thanks. a little messy in the roll out cause a couple of conf files - but overall great job.

[00:50] Liam Patel: yeah and to add, the autoscaler adjustments for Dedicated helped smoothing queueing during peak by roughly 18% spike capacity. it's not perfect yet but directionally good.

[01:10] Olivia Ruiz: customer side - we closed a midmarket expansion with NovaHealth this quarter, they moved their pilot to dedicated, signed a 12-month commit. big props to solutions eng and legal for moving fast.

[01:35] Avery Chen: nice - that's the type of signal we need. numbers wise - revenue beat plan by 7% this quarter, net retention remains strong, and gross margin on hosted climbed 3 points because of batching and better quantization profiles on a subset of tiers.

[02:05] Noah Kim: on product - roadmap highlights: 1) Private (VPC + on-prem) GA timeline remains end of Q2, still on track pending a few compliance signoffs; 2) Redwood Optimize features - initial rollout of model recommendation engine to a subset of customers in April; 3) Console improvements for tracing and cost breakdowns are in beta next week.

[02:40] Maya Alvarez: technical note - we're prioritizing two runtime improvements: the KV cache eviction policy tweak and optimized kernel selection for 8-bit quantized ops. these should help medium-length chats where we saw perf regressions. expect PRs and internal benchmarks next week.

[03:05] Priya Shah: hiring - we're targeting +25 headcount this quarter, TBH we gotta be more efficient. focus on infra, se, and customer reliability engineers. interview experience improvements rolling out; new scorecards go live Monday.

[03:30] Olivia Ruiz: sales motion - PLG still core but we've added targeted enterprise plays for healthcare and finance, with dedicated enablement packs. pipeline is healthy but longer sales cycles in regulated verticals - need SSO, SOC2, localized data residency.

[03:55] Audience Q: (crowd) what's the plan for security?

[04:05] Maya Alvarez: security update - SOC 2 Type II report cleared in Feb, ISO path underway, we've added KMS integration for Private and Dedicated, and internal audit logs now retained for 365 days for enterprise tiers. still working on some FedRAMP-related questions for a couple of prospects, but we have a plan.

[04:35] Liam Patel: to add on reliability - new fallback policy is in place that will route to compatible model variants when capacity is low; we saw that trigger once in staging and it fell back gracefully. we need to tighten the metrics so we can detect false positives.

[05:00] Avery Chen: ok let's call out a few company-level priorities for next quarter: 1) nail Private deployment rollout and customer onboarding; 2) improve unit economics on hosted via Optimize (batching/caching recommendations); 3) scale Dedicated sales plays; 4) invest in reliability and observability.

[05:28] Audience member (Leah - Eng): question - are we going to broaden supported hardware profiles for Dedicated?

[05:40] Liam Patel: good q - yes, roadmap includes support for next-gen accelerator configs but timing depends on partner availability and kernel work. we'll share details in the infra town next week.

[06:05] Noah Kim: can I add - product will start a cross-functional pilot next week to test the new model recommendation flow on 5 customers; engineering + se will run it. we'll track unit cost changes and quality regressions.

[06:30] Audience Q (Jake - Sales): what are the top objections we're seeing in demos?

[06:40] Olivia Ruiz: latency vs cost is top, then security reqs (SSO, audit logs), sometimes customers ask for on-prem fully air-gapped. we usually propose Dedicated + Private option and offer a pilot to run benchmarks. pricing transparency and unit economics conversation helps.

[07:00] Avery Chen: small behavioral note - when demoing, emphasize predictable SLAs and the rollback/rollout tooling for model versioning. that helps with procurement.

[07:20] Maya Alvarez: ops update - cost optimization: caching now active for 40% of requests where we can safely reuse prefixes. that saved tokens but also highlighted some edge cases where cache invalidation caused stale outputs; engineers are addressing.

[07:50] Audience Q (remote): can we get an update on global regions?

[08:00] Liam Patel: we're ramping EU region capacity, APAC is pilot-phase with partners; expect CER-level availability in EU next month. APAC expansion is slower due to partner integrations.

[08:25] Priya Shah: people update - new parental leave policy and expanded mental health days; also an internal reorg for CS to create a Solutions Engineering track.

[08:45] Avery Chen: quick customer story - NovaHealth used Redwood Dedicated to reduce inference cost by 30% compared to their initial hosted pilot, while hitting latency SLOs. their security team liked the audit logs and KMS integration.

[09:10] Audience Q (Marta - Research): are we open to contributing to open-source inference kernels?

[09:20] Maya Alvarez: yes but with guardrails. we want to upstream non-sensitive perf improvements, but model-specific kernel code tied to proprietary IP will remain internal. looking to balance community contributions and competitive differentiation.

[09:40] Q&A rapid fire - several managers asked for a managers' sync on hiring and OKR alignment, product asked for prioritized customer lists for Private early access.

[10:05] Avery Chen: ok closing items - we will share a slide deck with detailed metrics by Friday; managers please schedule alignment meetings. thank you everyone, appreciate the hustle.

[10:20] Outro music / chatter as meeting ends.

Notes: transcription imperfect in spots; some words garbled (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "kay vee cache" in places). Links shared during the call: Q1 metrics deck (internal link), Private deployment RFC (internal link), Hiring plan doc (internal link).
